### (1) Per-claim replication assessment

- **C1 — AGREE.** Replication reports **exactly** 3,190,226 bp and **GC 40.09%**, with contig structure consistent with 1 chromosome (~3.07 Mb) + plasmids, and FLUB is largest among the sampled L. hilgardii genomes.
- **C2 — PARTIAL.** Gene-content totals do **not** match numerically (Prokka 2991 CDS vs paper 2871 CDS; paper also reports RNAs/pseudogenes), but the discrepancy is plausibly due to annotation pipeline differences; qualitative “high gene count” holds.
- **C3 — PARTIAL.** Pangenome totals are close but not identical (4089 vs 4181 clusters; core fraction 48.9% vs 49.3%); overall structure (≈half core, remainder variable) is reproduced, but exact counts are not.
- **C4 — AGREE (near-exact).** FLUB singleton genes are essentially reproduced (268–269 vs 266), supporting “many unique genes” and compatibility with an open pangenome; however, “carries the most unique genes” is slightly weakened because LMG07934 is comparable in the replication.
- **C5 — PARTIAL.** Closest-neighbor relationship is broadly consistent (FLUB closest to the ATCC27305/LMG07934 group at very high ANI), but the “all ≥97%” floor is not strictly met (some pairs ~96.9%), and the exact “99.9%” figure is not reproduced (99.77% here).
- **C6 — PARTIAL.** dDDH was not recomputed, so the **numeric** dDDH claim (76.5%, most similar to ATCC8290 by dDDH) is unverified; species membership is strongly supported indirectly by ANI.

### (2) Coverage and agreement
- **Coverage:** **6/6** (each claim was addressed, though some only indirectly).
- **Agreement:** **2/6 agree**, **4/6 partial**, **0/6 disagree**.

### (3) VERDICT: **PARTIAL**
Core genomic size/GC (C1) and FLUB’s high singleton count (C4) replicate very well, and the pangenome/ANI patterns are broadly consistent. However, several key numeric results depend on pipeline-specific annotation (C2), different pangenome tool settings (C3), or an unrun method (dDDH in C6), leaving multiple headline numbers not independently reproduced exactly.
